author: simulation_agent

targets.note: the person's, 2026-09-23: recover the known stiffness to one per cent. RELATIVE, and on the RECOVERED-OVER-INPUT RATIO rather than on a stiffness in pN/um -- that is what makes the target well posed against an E3 viscosity, since the same drag coefficient imposes the offset and inverts it and eta cancels out of the ratio. A target is a decision and carries no grade (5.3.1)

numbers.name: bead_diameter
numbers.note: the SI anchor: the particle in the bottle, measured directly. Sets the drag through Stokes and the soft end of the stiffness sweep through the thermal width

numbers.name: temperature
numbers.note: a parameter of the noise amplitude and realised exactly by the model, not a thermostat setpoint. The room's reading; nothing actuates the sample (kb:sample_temperature_not_actuated)

numbers.name: viscosity
numbers.note: pure water, validity 288 to 298 K and the temperature above is inside it. THE ENTRY SAYS `of order` one mPa s, so this is one significant figure and the precision below says so

numbers.name: diffusivity
numbers.note: the free diffusivity of the anchor sphere. Here it is not the observable but the noise scale: it sets how long the offset must be averaged

numbers.name: diffusive_time
numbers.note: kb:tau_d's relation, carried for CONTRAST and not as a bound. Under a trap it is no longer the shortest characteristic time, and the two relaxation times below are two to five decades under it -- which is exactly why bd_overdamped's A1 cannot be reused here

numbers.name: trap_stiffness_min
numbers.note: the soft end of the range the person set on 2026-09-23. A decision, not an estimate; assumed: is the nearest source kind because a decision can be named by reference only when it is a target or an envelope limit

numbers.name: trap_stiffness_max
numbers.note: the stiff end of the person's range: two decades, so three stiffness levels a decade apart

numbers.name: sigma_over_diameter_soft_corner
numbers.note: the thermal width at the soft end as a fraction of the diameter. Revision 3 ASSUMED this and derived the soft stiffness from it; now the stiffness is the person's and this is derived from it

numbers.name: trap_relaxation_time_max
numbers.note: gamma/k_t at the soft end: the longest relaxation time, which sets the record length

numbers.name: trap_relaxation_time_min
numbers.note: gamma/k_t at the stiff end: the shortest characteristic time, which sets the timestep

numbers.name: offset_over_sigma_min
numbers.note: the dimensionless sweep variable is the offset in thermal widths, gamma*v/sqrt(k_B*temperature*trap_stiffness), because that and not the speed is what sets the per-frame signal to noise. At 1 the offset is buried in the fluctuation and only averaging recovers it

numbers.name: offset_over_sigma_max
numbers.note: two decades up, where a single frame already shows the offset. The SPEED this becomes depends on the stiffness, so the speed is an A7 interval per corner and not one number here

numbers.name: deviation_limit_in_standard_errors
numbers.note: the person's choice on 2026-09-23: a cell's recovered stiffness passes when it differs from the declared one by at most three of that cell's own standard errors. A decision, carried as assumed: because a decision can be named by reference only when it is a target or an envelope limit

assumptions.statement: The stiffness range, 0.1 to 10 pN/um, was set by the person on 2026-09-23 in answer to the question revision 3 left open. It replaces revision 3's derived corners (0.02 and 20 pN/um, from a thermal width of a tenth of a diameter). It is a decision and not an estimate.
assumptions.falsifier: the person changing the range, which is a revision and not a correction

assumptions.statement: The person has not given a speed range. Sweeping the speed directly would confound two things, because the same speed is a large offset in a soft trap and an invisible one in a stiff one. The dimensionless offset in thermal widths is what the statistics depend on, so the sweep is stated in it and A7 turns it into a speed interval at each stiffness. One to a hundred spans buried-in-noise to visible-per-frame.
assumptions.falsifier: a person's speed range replaces both ends; and on the bench the upper end is cut by trap escape, which this purely harmonic model cannot see and A7 records as a limit of the model rather than of the protocol

assumptions.statement: Revision 4's accuracy criterion -- recovered within one per cent -- was met by a correct integrator only about three cells in four, because the cells' own error is near one per cent; in both attempts one cell of six missed, a different one each time. The person replaced it with a limit of three standard errors, under which a correct cell misses about 0.3 per cent of the time and six cells about 2 per cent.
assumptions.falsifier: a cell outside three standard errors in two independent seeds is a systematic error, not noise

kb_refs.claim: The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.
The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's.
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.

constraint_notes: revision 5 cites revision 4 as a record and does not take it as input (4.5.5). WHAT MOVED: the person replaced the accuracy criterion. Precision stays the one per cent relative uncertainty target; accuracy is now a deviation of at most three of the cell's own standard errors, where it was within one per cent. The stiffness range, 0.1-10 pN/um, and the speed sweep are revision 4's.

the person's question, verbatim in intent: a single Brownian particle confined by a harmonic optical trap U = (1/2)*k_t*dr^2, with the surrounding fluid moving at constant velocity relative to the trap; how the steady-state displacement depends on the imposed speed for different trap stiffnesses, the relationship between speed, viscous drag and displacement, how it changes over a range of stiffnesses, and whether the known stiffness can be recovered from the simulated drag-calibration measurement

revision 3 ran one smoke cell and not the grid, because the plan checker could not read a window that varies per sweep point and the per-step cost was a bracket three decades wide. The checker now reads sweep points, and the smoke runs measured about 2 us a step at one particle on both engines, so this revision plans the grid.

the recovered stiffness is NOT evidence about any trap: gamma and k_t both go in and the estimator inverts the equation the integrator solved. What the grid tests is the error model -- that the fractional error of the recovered stiffness is sqrt(2*tau/T)/(offset/sigma) with the stiffness cancelled -- across two decades of stiffness, which one cell could not.
still open for the person: the speed range the stage can command, and whether a maximum trap force belongs in the model (a different configuration, not a setting)
